notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-18T07:40Z: the sibling create_test_case_comment probe created comment id 1307 on TC-54458 (the exact 0-baseline triple: project 379335744 / folder 764828 / test_case 1975349). Re-invoked this capability on that same triple (attempt 3) and independently confirmed count 0 -> 1, with the real row: {id:1307, user_id:{id:2522,full_name:'ing',email:'probe-user@example.invalid'}, group_id:2615, project_id:379335744, parent_id:null, entity_id:1975349, entity_type:'TestCase', created_at:'2026-09-18T07:36:43.727Z', comment:'__mcp-probe-comment-2026-09-18T07:36:35Z', edited:false, is_editable:true}.

Field-by-field, every declared field is PRESENT with the correct type (id, user_id.{id,full_name,email}, group_id, project_id, parent_id, entity_id, entity_type, created_at, comment, edited, is_editable) and there are no undeclared fields. review_status is absent but that is declared conditional behaviour (only present on review-verdict comments) — correctly NOT counted as declared_missing.

However the VALUES of two fields contradict their own guidance, independently confirming what the sibling create-probe found:
- entity_type returned 'TestCase', not the schema's own example 'TRTC', and guidance explicitly describes it as "'TRTC' for a comment on a test case inside a test run" — this comment was added directly on a test case, not inside a run, and the value reflects that, so either the guidance/example is stale or this capability only ever sees the TestCase variant on this kind of case. Either way, guidance contradicts the observed response, which per this suite's standing rule counts as a reportable DRIFT even though the schema's field/type match.
- entity_id returned 1975349, which is exactly the test_case_id — not "the id of the run/case mapping cell" the schema describes it as. Same DRIFT category: the field is present and correctly typed, but the guidance describing what it MEANS is false for this path.

Both of these were flagged by the sibling create_test_case_comment probe and are now independently confirmed via this read endpoint on the same row — this is drift on two capabilities sharing the same underlying comment shape, not a one-off in the write path.

Flat vs nested schema disagreement (pattern evidence per this suite's standing lesson, not itself scored as drift): group_id, project_id and parent_id all appear in the nested per-comment schema and in the real response, but are absent from this capability's own flat `returns` array (which lists only: comments, id, comment, user_id, entity_id, entity_type, created_at, edited, is_editable, success, info). The flat `returns` list under-reports the nested shape — consistent with the suite-wide finding that the flat returns array is unreliable in both directions.

Sample-size caveat: this is verified against exactly ONE real comment (id 1307), created by this test suite. Fields that only populate under other circumstances remain unexercised: parent_id under real threading (this route's guidance says it is 'always null through this path', so a non-null value may never be observable here), edited=true after an actual edit, and review_status on a review-verdict comment. Newest-first-on-page-1 and 'archived case still returns comments' guidance also remain unexercised (only one comment exists, and the case is not archived).

Verdict: DRIFT. Top-level envelope and all field presences/types are correct (that part would be PASS in isolation), but the guidance-contradicting values of entity_type and entity_id are a reportable drift per the standing rule that guidance disagreeing with the response counts even when the schema shape matches. Severity: low-to-moderate — nothing is absent or malformed, but any caller following the guidance's description of entity_id/entity_type (e.g. to distinguish run-scoped vs. bare test-case comments) will get a wrong mental model from a real response.
